newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian blue chips head lower in flooded market.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian blue chips head lower in flooded market.

text.p: Shares of leading Nigerian firms finished lower in active trade on Tuesday as more blue chips flooded the market, dealers said.
The all-share index slipped a tiny bit to 6570.51 from 6570.52 on Monday.
Nigerian Breweries dropped 30 kobo to 11.80 naira while Guinness lost 29 kobo to 7.80 naira.
Cadbury had five kobo shaved off to end at 26.75 naira, the same as United Bank for Africa which closed at 5.10 naira.
Conglomerate UAC fell by 10 kobo to 10.10 naira, while Vitafoam slid 10 kobo to 4.30 naira.
Hospital group Ekocorp was the biggest loser, finishing 50 kobo lower after adjusting for dividend payment and scrip issue.
It finished at 2.22 naira on the news that it would pay 20 kobo and a scrip of one new share for every eight.
But sustained demand saw bank shares up. New comer on the exchange Guaranty Trust Bank jumped to 14.00 naira, gaining 25 kobo while NAL Merchant Bank added 10 kobo to 5.20 naira.
Nestle Foods soared 40 kobo to 34.00 naira and Union Dicon Salt garnered 20 kobo to end at 36.00 naira.
Oil shares Unipetrol and Mobil gained 20 kobo each to 42.00 naira and 39.50 naira, respectively.
Insurance companies fared well, led by AIICO which rose by five kobo to 7.20 naira. Prestige Assurance gained three to 4.80 naira and Niger Insurance added two kobo to 2.47 naira.
Despite an improved full year result, packaging firm Avon Crowncaps was unchanged at 4.00 naira, indicating lack of interest in the sector, a trader said.
